uncited: *   **Inputs:** Network parameters $\theta$, learning rate $\eta$, location vectors $\{x_j\}$, outgoing directions $\{\omega_j\}$, incident directions $\{\omega_{in,j,k}\}$, and reference radiance values.
*   **Radiance Prediction Network:** A multi-layer perceptron (MLP) consisting of seven linear layers, each with 512 units.
The method replaces the standard L2 loss gradient with a semi-gradient estimator.
The baseline minimizes the L2 distance between the left-hand side (LHS, outgoing radiance $L_\theta$) and the right-hand side (RHS, sum of emitted and reflected radiance $\langle R_\theta \rangle$).

*   **Bias in Baseline:** The baseline method is a biased estimator because of the correlation between $\nabla_\theta \langle R_\theta \rangle$ and $\langle R_\theta \rangle$ in the partial derivative with respect to the RHS.
*   **Convergence Guarantee:** Due to mathematical shortcomings in the definition of the stop-gradient operation, convergence of the L2-form loss cannot be prematurely guaranteed.
A technique to expedite initial convergence by integrating neural path guiding.
Faster convergence and lower final error.
*   **When to use:** When training neural radiance caches for global illumination rendering and fast convergence is desired.
